ai.literal: Enduring the pain that comes upon oneself, and not doing harm to other lives, is indeed of that nature which is the true form of penance.
ai.translation: To endure the suffering that comes upon oneself and to refrain from causing harm to any living being—this is the true form of penance.
ai.modern: தனக்கு வரும் துன்பங்களைப் பொறுத்துக் கொள்வதும், பிற உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதுமே தவத்தின் உண்மையான வடிவமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature and form of penance (தவம்). It consists of two essential aspects: first, 'நோன்றல்' (enduring) the 'உற்றநோய்' (pain or hardships that come upon oneself), and second, 'செய்யாமை' (not doing) 'உறுகண்' (harm or distress) to any 'உயிர்க்கு' (living being). The word 'உரு' here means the true form or essence, indicating that penance is not merely an external ritual but an internal discipline of patience and non-violence. Together, these two practices constitute the complete definition of ascetic virtue.

ai.literal: Even penance to those who possess penance will succeed; that, those who lack that, undertaking [is in vain].
ai.translation: Austerity is possible only for those who have already acquired the capacity for it; for those who lack it, undertaking it is in vain.
ai.modern: தவம் செய்யும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களுக்கே தவம் கைகூடும்; அந்த ஆற்றல் இல்லாதவர்கள் தவத்தை மேற்கொள்வது வீணான முயற்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that true penance or self-discipline (தவம்) is not an easy task that anyone can perform on a whim. It is only successful for those who already possess the spiritual strength and discipline (தவமுடையார்) required for it. For those who lack this inner preparation (அஃதிலார்), merely attempting to undertake it (மேற்கொள்வது) is a futile effort. The poet emphasizes that the very capacity to perform austerity is itself a hard-won quality.

ai.literal: To those who renounced, sustenance desiring, did they forget, perhaps, the other people, penance?
ai.translation: Perhaps other people forgot to perform penance themselves because they needed to provide sustenance to those who have renounced.
ai.modern: துறந்தவர்களுக்கு உணவு மற்றும் உதவிகளைச் செய்ய வேண்டியிருப்பதால் தான், மற்றவர்கள் தவம் செய்வதை மறந்துவிட்டார்களோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the essential relationship between householders and ascetics. The poet rhetorically asks if ordinary people forgot to perform penance because they were occupied with providing sustenance to those who have renounced. If everyone abandoned worldly life to perform penance, there would be no one left to support them. Thus, the householder's duty of charity is shown to be as vital as the ascetic's penance.

ai.literal: Enemies destroying and loved ones prospering and, if one considers, through penance will come.
ai.translation: If one considers, both the power to destroy one's enemies and the power to elevate one's friends are attained through the strength of penance.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், பகைவர்களை அழிப்பதும் அன்பானவர்களை உயர்த்துவதும் தவ வலிமையால் மட்டுமே கைக்கூடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet highlights the immense, dual power of penance (தவம்). It states that if one deeply reflects (எண்ணின்), both the ability to punish or destroy adversaries (ஒன்னார்த் தெறலும்) and the ability to bless or elevate loved ones (உவந்தாரை ஆக்கலும்) are acquired through the power of penance (தவத்தான் வரும்). The word 'தெறல்' means to destroy or burn, indicating the destructive power of a sage's wrath, while 'ஆக்கல்' means to create or prosper, indicating their power to bless. Thus, penance is not merely passive endurance but a source of supreme spiritual power that can affect the external world in both destructive and constructive ways.

ai.literal: Because one attains the desired things in the very manner desired, the penance performed must be practiced here in this world.
ai.translation: Since one can attain whatever they desire, in the exact manner they desire it, penance is something that must be diligently practiced here in this life.
ai.modern: விரும்பியவற்றை விரும்பியவாறே பெற முடியும் என்பதால், தவம் செய்வதை இவ்வுலகிலேயே மேற்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme efficacy of penance. The poet explains that through penance, a person can obtain whatever they wish for, exactly in the way they wished to obtain it. Because of this immense power to fulfill one's deepest aspirations, the practice of penance is highly recommended to be undertaken diligently in this very life. The word 'vēṇṭiyāṅku' combines 'vēṇṭi' and 'āṅku' to emphasize that the result matches the desire perfectly.

ai.literal: Those who do penance do their own duty; others who do not, having fallen within desire, do ruin.
ai.translation: Those who perform penance are the ones who truly perform their own duty; all others, caught in the grip of desire, only bring about their own ruin.
ai.modern: தவம் செய்கின்றவர்களே தங்களுக்குரிய கடமையைச் செய்கின்றவர்கள் ஆவர்; அவ்வாறு செய்யாத மற்றவர்கள் ஆசையில் சிக்கித் தங்களுக்குக் கேடு விளைவித்துக் கொள்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true nature of duty and action. It states that those who practice penance (tavam) are the only ones who are actually performing their true duty (karumam), as they master themselves. On the other hand, those who do not practice penance are trapped by worldly desires (ācai) and end up doing things that lead to waste or ruin (avam). The contrast between 'karumam' (meaningful duty/action) and 'avam' (wasteful/harmful action) highlights that self-control is essential for any meaningful life endeavor.

words.gloss: to those who are able to practice penance

ai.literal: Like gold that shines more as it is heated and emits luster, to those who practice penance as suffering burns and burns them.
ai.translation: Just as gold shines more brilliantly the more it is heated in fire, the spiritual luster of those who perform penance increases the more they are purified by the sufferings they undergo.
ai.modern: நெருப்பில் சுடச்சுட ஒளிவிடுகின்ற பொன்னைப் போல, துன்பங்கள் வருத்த வருத்தத் தவம் மேற்கொள்பவர்களுக்கு அறிவு மற்றும் ஆற்றல் ஒளி பெருகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the practice of penance to the refining of gold. Gold becomes purer and shines more brilliantly each time it is heated in fire. Similarly, those who practice penance find their inner spiritual strength and wisdom growing greater and brighter with every suffering they endure. The repetition of 'சுடச்சுட' (as it burns) emphasizes the continuous nature of both the refining process and the endurance of hardships.

ai.literal: Him who has attained the state where his own soul is severed from ego, all other abiding living beings will worship.
ai.translation: All other living beings will worship him who has attained complete mastery over his own soul by severing it from egoistic attachment.
ai.modern: தன் உயிரை தன் முனைப்பு அல்லது அகந்தை நீங்குமாறு ஆளப் பெற்றவனை, உலகில் நிலைபெற்றுள்ள மற்ற எல்லா உயிர்களும் வணங்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the spiritual power and universal reverence achieved through true penance. The phrase 'tannuyir tān aṟa' refers to severing the ego or the false sense of 'I' (tāṉ) from one's own soul (uyir). When an ascetic achieves this state of complete self-mastery and detachment, they transcend ordinary human limitations. Consequently, all other living beings ('maṉṉuyir ellām') in the world will naturally revere and bow down to them.

ai.literal: Death escaping even will be achieved, through penance's power to those who have attained.
ai.translation: Even escaping death is possible for those who have attained the power of penance.
ai.modern: தவத்தின் வலிமையைப் பெற்றவர்களுக்கு, எமனைக் கடந்து உயிர் பிழைப்பதும் சாத்தியமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme power of penance. The author states that those who have successfully attained the spiritual strength and power that comes from practicing penance can achieve anything, even overcoming or escaping death itself. The word 'கூற்றம்' refers to death, and 'குதித்தல்' means to leap over or escape. The phrase 'கைகூடும்' emphasizes that such an extraordinary feat becomes easily attainable for them. Thus, the couplet illustrates that the power of self-discipline and austerity transcends even the ultimate physical limitation of mortality.

those who do not perform penance

ai.literal: The reason why those who have not are many is that those who perform penance are few, and those who do not perform penance are many.
ai.translation: The reason why the destitute are so numerous in this world is that those who practice self-discipline are very few, while those who do not are many.
ai.modern: உலகில் வறியவர்கள் பலராக இருப்பதற்குக் காரணம், தவம் (சுயகட்டுப்பாடு) மேற்கொள்பவர்கள் சிலராகவும், அதனை மேற்கொள்ளாதவர்கள் பலராகவும் இருப்பதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the disparity in human achievement and well-being through the lens of self-discipline or penance (tavam). The poet states that the reason why there are so many 'have-nots' (ilar) in the world is directly linked to a lack of effort and self-restraint. Those who undergo the rigorous practice of penance (nōṟpār) are very few, whereas those who avoid such discipline (nōlātavar) make up the vast majority. By equating the lack of penance with being a 'have-not', the couplet emphasizes that true wealth, power, and success are the fruits of sustained self-discipline and endurance.
